report:
Reviewed the full completeness claim, three ordinary implementation associations (method.rs, resolve/mod.rs, local_syms/mods.rs), the explicit TODO implementation association, and both associated test entries. Captured test setup and relevant BuiltinDeriveTcx metadata context. This anchor remains partially implemented and partially tested; the TODO is essential to that assessment.

The claim requires represented alternatives and exhaustiveness to remain separate, and forbids treating an incomplete empty source as a definitive negative. traits_in_method_scope returns represented trait identities, per-provider definite-scope flags, and a separate scope-complete boolean. It retains represented traits while marking uncertainty for failed imports, local-glob provider enumeration, missing or ambiguous edition preludes, and incomplete module expansion. local_syms/mods.rs checks unresolved/unsupported/depth-limited bang expansion, active attributes, parse errors and applicable derive handling rather than equating the finite expanded-item vector with a complete directory. Method-provider completeness has its own policy. Thus the source of uncertainty remains independent of candidates which expansion already produced.

method.rs consumes that pair: unknown starts from !scope_complete plus unhandled bound/inherent providers; unsupported signatures and Maybe trait goals preserve unknown instead of becoming No. Definite candidates are accumulated separately. Selection requires exactly one definite candidate and !unknown. Multiple definite candidates yield ambiguity; otherwise unknown yields the explicit incomplete-candidate diagnostic; only the remaining exhaustive zero-candidate branch reports no applicable method. The external-inherent path checks completeness before treating an empty candidate list as absence. The changed generated import-root audit in resolve/mod.rs compares identities/provenance and leaves these completeness propagation paths intact.

The ordinary test unresolved_item_macro_keeps_method_scope_incomplete visibly supplies unknown_items! alongside a Clone-derived type and checks the selected method body for an incomplete-candidate-information diagnostic. It exercises a represented candidate together with an unresolved expansion, detecting the common error of selecting a known candidate while ignoring possible missing providers. It does not prove the incomplete-empty case or the complete absent/unique/ambiguous matrix. Its assertion checks diagnostic presence, not exclusivity; that limitation is not treated as exhaustive coverage.

The TODO implementation entry explicitly states that a uniform completeness result across all lookup forms is not implemented; ordinary resolve_path still returns alternatives alone. The TODO test explicitly requires absent, unique, ambiguous and incomplete fixtures, particularly incomplete empty provider sets and exhaustive-empty negative reasoning. This adequately accounts for the remaining broad claim instead of pretending the method-provider slice satisfies every lookup form. Completing it requires a common explicit result protocol and targeted assertions across those states. There are no N/A entries.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib unresolved_item_macro_keeps_method_scope_incomplete: one test passed, 144 filtered out, with existing compiler warnings. This execution supplements source review only for that scenario. No production or test sources changed. No requested edits; accepted deferrals remain visibly TODO.
